3942af6e20054b6c.description:
Institutional Equities | Equity Research Associate
Location: BKC, Mumbai
Experience: Minimum 2 years of relevant Equity Research experience
Qualification: MBA (Finance) / CA
Function: Institutional Equities – Research
Employment Type: Full-time
About the Role
We are looking for a Research Associate to join our Institutional Equities Research team. The candidate will be responsible for conducting detailed fundamental research across sectors such as Chemicals, IT, Internet, Defence, Capital Goods, and Real Estate.
The role requires strong financial analysis, industry understanding, modelling capabilities, and the ability to translate research into actionable investment insights for institutional clients.
Key Responsibilities
1. Sector & Company Research
• Conduct detailed fundamental research on companies across assigned sectors.
• Track industry trends, regulatory developments, competitive dynamics, and key growth drivers.
• Develop a strong understanding of sector-specific business models and operating metrics.
• Monitor company announcements, earnings updates, management commentary, industry developments, and macroeconomic factors.
• Identify key risks, opportunities, catalysts, and potential investment themes.
2. Financial Analysis & Modelling
• Build and maintain detailed financial models covering P&L, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow.
• Perform historical financial analysis and develop forward-looking estimates.
• Conduct valuation analysis using methodologies such as DCF, P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B and SOTP, as relevant.
• Analyse earnings quality, margins, working capital, cash flows, capital allocation and return ratios.
• Track quarterly performance against estimates and revise forecasts where required.
• Conduct sensitivity and scenario analysis to assess key business drivers.
3. Equity Research Reports
• Assist in preparing initiation reports, result updates, sector reports, thematic reports and company notes.
• Develop investment theses supported by detailed financial and industry analysis.
• Prepare earnings previews and post-result analysis.
• Generate concise and insightful research outputs for institutional investors.
• Ensure research reports are accurate, data-driven and supported by appropriate analysis.
4. Industry & Competitive Analysis
• Conduct peer benchmarking and comparative analysis.
• Track market share, pricing trends, capacity additions, order books, utilisation levels and other relevant sector-specific KPIs.
• Identify emerging industry trends and assess their impact on covered companies.
• Track competitor performance and strategic developments.
5. Management & Industry Interaction
• Participate in management interactions, earnings calls, analyst meets and investor conferences.
• Prepare relevant questions and discussion points for management interactions.
• Capture key takeaways and assess their impact on investment assumptions.
• Interact with industry experts and other relevant stakeholders to strengthen sector understanding.
6. Data & Research Support
• Gather, validate and analyse financial and industry data from credible sources.
• Maintain databases for companies, sectors, peers and key operating metrics.
• Track company disclosures, regulatory filings, investor presentations, conference calls and annual reports.
• Ensure timely availability of research inputs for senior analysts.
7. Collaboration with Senior Analysts
• Work closely with the Senior Analyst / Research Head on sector coverage and investment ideas.
• Support the development of investment recommendations and sector views.
• Take ownership of assigned companies and gradually develop independent research capabilities.
• Present key findings and investment insights to the research team.
Sector Coverage
The candidate may be aligned to one or more of the following sectors:
• Chemicals
• Information Technology (IT)
• Internet / New Economy
• Defence
• Capital Goods
• Real Estate
Required Skills & Competencies
• Strong understanding of Fundamental Equity Research.
• Good knowledge of financial statements and accounting principles.
• Strong financial modelling and valuation skills.
• Ability to analyse businesses and develop an independent investment view.
• Strong Excel and financial analysis skills.
• Good understanding of equity markets and capital markets.
• Excellent research and analytical capabilities.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to interpret large amounts of information and identify key investment drivers.
• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
Eligibility Criteria
Minimum Experience:
• 2+ years of relevant experience in Equity Research / Institutional Equity Research.
Educational Qualification:
• MBA / PGDM – Finance from a reputed institute, OR
• Chartered Accountant (CA).
Preferred Background:
• Candidates currently working in Institutional Equity Research, Brokerage Research, Investment Banks, Asset Management Companies, PMS/AIFs or other buy-side/sell-side research platforms.
• Candidates with direct sector coverage experience in Chemicals, IT, Internet, Defence, Capital Goods or Real Estate will be preferred.
Key Performance Indicators
Success in the role will be evaluated based on:
• Quality and accuracy of research output.
• Timeliness of research reports and earnings updates.
• Quality of financial models and forecasts.
• Depth of sector and company understanding.
• Ability to identify investment opportunities and risks.
• Contribution to investment ideas and research themes.
• Quality of management/industry insights.
• Responsiveness to internal and institutional client requirements.
Location
BKC, Mumbai
Experience: Minimum 2 years relevant experience
Qualification: MBA / CA
Function: Institutional Equities – Equity Research

Drive Time-to-Live (TTL) and Time-to-First-Value (TTFV) for every account in your portfolio. Project-manage implementations end-to-end. Codify what’s working into repeatable playbooks. Personalise onboarding to each merchant’s specific objectives. Build durable two-way engagement. Engage proactively and contextually based on merchant-health signals such as app actions, sessions, ROI, revenue, and conversion. Maintain a predictable cadence and ensure every touchpoint delivers something the merchant didn’t already know. The bar: 80%+ of your portfolio in active two-way engagement at any given time. Make adoption predictable. Know our solutions end-to-end, including the platform direction . Map them to each merchant’s objectives and build adoption plans they actually want to follow. Help merchants take their first deliberate steps into intent-led commerce — even when they haven’t named the problem yet. Operate with leverage, not activity. Use Swym’s AI-native tooling as a force multiplier on your work. AI agents draft your QBR narratives and surface patterns across your portfolio in seconds. Custom workflows handle your renewal-prep packets, your call summaries, your follow-ups, your account documentation. The expectation: throughput and account quality that wouldn’t be achievable any other way. Drive feature adoption with evidence. Identify the most-valued features for each customer segment, build adoption playbooks around them, and benchmark outcomes. Share what’s working back to PLG, Product, and Marketing — backed by data, not anecdotes. Run clean handovers and contract hygiene. Enforce SOPs for handover from Sales — no context leaks. Every account in your portfolio has its contract logged in HubSpot. Be a teammate. Collaborate cleanly with Product, Support, Marketing, Sales, and our agency partners. Help Sales preempt renewals and make expansion forecasting predictable. Represent Swym’s evolution. As the platform grows from solutions-as-features to solutions-as-the-defining-layer of the brand experience, your customers need a guide. That’s you. Requirements Non-negotiable * 3–5 years in customer-facing roles — ideally Customer Success or Customer Support at a SaaS company. * Genuinely happy about helping people. If we could only name one trait that defined success in this role, this would be it. * AI-native operating capability. You use Claude, ChatGPT, or similar tools as a force multiplier on your work — not as a novelty or an experiment. You prompt, iterate, and build workflows. You know when to delegate to an agent and when human judgment is required. This is assessed in the interview, not assumed. * Excellent written and spoken English. Most of our customers aren’t in India, and you’ll handle hard conversations. * Tech-savvy. Comfortable in CRMs (HubSpot), with an affinity for web technologies — basic HTML, CSS, and JS. * Data-driven by default. Analysing merchant health and making decisions from it is second nature to you. * Organised. You’ll juggle a real portfolio with real complexity: prioritisation is a core skill. * Given our global presence, flexibility to operate across multiple time zones is required. Strongly preferred * Bachelor’s in Business Administration, Engineering, or similar. An MBA is a plus. * Familiarity with and how SaaS apps get evaluated and adopted there. * Experience with marketing automation stacks (Klaviyo, Attentive, Yotpo, Omnisend) — especially the data flow between intent capture tools and downstream campaigns. * Existing fluency with intent capture, email marketing automation, or shopper engagement as a product category. What Doesn’t Fit “Activity-led” CS profiles who measure themselves on touchpoints rather than outcomes. Operators who haven’t meaningfully adopted AI in their workflow — not because we require a specific tool set, but because the leverage expectation in this role demands it. Anyone whose strength is process compliance over judgment. The role rewards judgment. What Success Looks Like in the First 12 Months Months 1–3 — Foundation * Portfolio of customer accounts ramped, with each merchant’s objectives, health baseline, and value thesis documented. * AI operating model established for your portfolio: account-health diagnostics automated, QBR-prep workflows running, call-summary follow-ups going out within hours, not days. * TTL and TTFV benchmarks set for every active implementation; first 3 implementations completed against benchmark. * Two-way engagement cadence established with every account in your portfolio. Months 4–6 — Momentum * 80%+ of portfolio in active two-way engagement. * 80%+ of portfolio achieving compelling ROI on Swym solutions. * Adoption playbooks built and live for at least 2 customer segments — replicable, agent-assisted, ready to scale to new CSMs. * Structured product-feedback loop running into Product and PLG. * First wave of Solution Builder / new platform-tier feature adoption underway across the portfolio. Months 7–12 — Scale * Portfolio churn contained well below the company benchmark; expansions outpacing churn. * You can name 3+ AI workflows you’ve built or refined that materially changed your throughput. * Renewal forecasts you provide to Sales come in within ±10% of actuals. * A more junior CSM joining the team can ramp on your portfolio in 4 weeks because your documentation, playbooks, and workflows are clean. How We Work Swym operates on a human-in-the-loop model. Agents research, draft, audit, and execute. Humans make strategy calls, write the response, and own the relationship. As a CSM you’ll work alongside AI teammates. This includes Agents for portfolio research, task execution, and merchant intelligence, as well as custom workflows for the recurring shape of CS work, and you’ll be expected to direct them effectively. This is not a role where you’ll wait for RevOps to pull your data, or for a manager to approve every comms draft. Outputs ship daily. Decisions are made from data. Leverage is the primary metric. Why This, Why Now The brands Swym serves are at the front edge of a structural shift in retail. Discovery is moving off the storefront and onto AI agents. First-party intent data is becoming the only reliable signal in a post-cookie world. Email open rates are declining and the brands that survive are the ones that know their shoppers — what they want, when they’re ready, and where they are in the journey. Swym sits at the centre of that shift, with 50,000+ customers, 500+ agency partners, and a data moat that widens every quarter. If you want to work AI-first, with a team that means it, on a problem that matters — this is your moment. Our Vibe We’re a close-knit, fully-remote crew that never forgot our scrappy startup roots. Trust is sacred. Teamwork is the superpower. Our data-driven culture is built around making our merchants the heroes of their own stories. Benefits Remote work: We’re a remote-first company — flexibility and freedom by default. Time off: 20 days PTO, 10 sick days, 12 wellness leaves, and 10 fixed holidays. Compensation: Competitive pay and stock options for everyone. Health & fitness: Full health coverage, including fitness classes. Employee Wellness & Assistance Program: Confidential professional counseling (because we all need a little help sometimes). Interview Process Resume Screening Round 1 - Introductory Questionnaire Round 2 - Screening Call Round 3 - Panel Call 1 — Introductory Call (30 min) Round 4 - Written Assignment + Presentation (AI-fluency assessed here) Round 5 - Panel Call 2 (45 min) Round 6 - Panel Call 3 (45 min) Round 7 - HR Call (45 min) Swym is a remote-first company. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive team.
